main_body: Thatched hip roof over a log-plank wall with a central door and two round shields
top_band: Thatch roof slope from rows 7 to 53 (gold #bc9a45 with lighter #d8bb68 course highlights and dark #7b5c22 course lines), under a dark ridge outline at rows 5-6. The roof is a large sloped surface that widens toward the eave and has tapered hip ends.
evidence: The roof reads as a large sloped top surface, as in the Beodeul house references. Its eave overhangs a darker wall (a dark row at about 54-55 separates the two), and the hip ends narrow toward the ridge. The wall is a vertical south face about 23 rows tall. The door has a timber frame, a stone threshold and a dark inset interior, so it is recessed rather than painted flat. The roof and wall both satisfy the 3/4 contract. No receding isometric side faces appear.

style.evidence: The thatch carries about 6 lightness steps (L 23, 54, 69, 95, 124, 154, 186) with per-course dark lines and light dashes that suggest straw texture. The log wall has vertical plank variation and the shields have a shaded rim and centre. The outline is a tinted dark brown (only 6% neutral dark edge pixels), not black. Measured facts: 8 colours per tile versus 11 and 18 for the references, 38 distinct colours versus 66 and 185, and 2% flat-fill coverage. This is a bit below the references but close to the stone one, and the thatch banding is repetitive but well crafted. It would sit acceptably next to the references.
